content.title: About
content.content: Raisin bread is a whole‑grain loaf that incorporates dried grapes (raisins) into the dough. It has a subtle sweet aroma, a soft crumb, and a faint caramel note from the raisins, making it popular for breakfast or a snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Raisins in the bread retain some of their vitamins and minerals, especially potassium and iron.
Traditional raisin breads are common in Mediterranean and Eastern European cuisines.
The natural sugars in raisins help keep the loaf moist for a longer time.
During baking, raisins can swell slightly, creating characteristic pockets in the crumb.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain flour and raisins provide dietary fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Raisins supply potassium, which aids heart and muscle function.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Raisins are a good plant source of iron, beneficial for blood formation.

items.title: Low glycemic impact
items.content: The combination of whole grains and dried fruit results in a slower rise in blood sugar compared with white bread.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Phenolic compounds in raisins have antioxidant properties that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Raisins increase the overall sugar level of the bread, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Bread made from wheat flour can trigger reactions in individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sulfite presence
items.content: Some manufacturers use sulfites to preserve raisin color; these can cause allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raisin bread can be enjoyed plain, toasted with butter, spread with cream cheese, used for sandwiches, French toast, or croutons. It pairs well with honey, nut butter, and cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bread in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, refrigerate or freeze it wrapped in plastic to prevent drying out.
